page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.6xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture and running on KVM hypervisors, the instance allocates 24 vCPUs across 12 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside 35 MB of L3 cache. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps. The instance contains no bundled local storage and includes no discrete GPUs, necessitating external block storage solutions for persistent data persistence.

Benchmark measurements indicate balanced multi-threaded performance contrasting with modest single-core throughput. The instance recorded a multi-core Geekbench score of 7,163.0 and a multi-core stress-ng result of 17,660.86, placing it squarely in the middle tier. In contrast, single-thread stress-ng reached 1,108.98 and single-core Geekbench logged 935.0, reflecting lower execution efficiency on single-threaded tasks such as gzip compression. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reached 96.89 GB/sec, while write operations measured 52.55 GB/sec.

From an operational tradeoff perspective, the ecs.se1ne.6xlarge prioritizes memory footprint and concurrent throughput over per-core burst capacity. The extensive 192 GB RAM pool supports substantial working sets, yet the absence of local NVMe storage limits raw I/O throughput to attached network disks. This architecture provides cost-effective density for RAM-intensive concurrent tasks, functioning effectively for in-memory caching solutions like Redis, relational database systems, ETL pipeline staging, and multi-threaded enterprise services.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.6xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 24 vCPUs and 192.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz on KVM. Reflecting an 8:1 memory-to-core allocation, the configuration integrates 12 physical cores with hyper-threading, 35 MB of L3 cache, and a 4 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, while omitting bundled local storage and hardware accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place the instance in the middle tier for multi-core performance, evidenced by a multi-core Geekbench score of 7,163.0 and stress-ng throughput of 17,660.86, counterbalanced by modest single-threaded metrics. The substantial RAM allocation paired with moderate parallel compute makes this instance technically suited for enterprise databases, in-memory caching systems, distributed data processing, and large memory-bound backend services requiring high capacity over extreme single-thread speed.
